messages:
maria: heads up — gatekeeper started rejecting toolcall responses from checkout-service. seeing a spike of `enum`-mismatch validation errors in the logs.
kevin: confirmed. model sometimes returns status values like 'failed' / 'error' / 'FAILED'. our schema expects STATUS: enum('OK','FAILED') uppercase. strict gatekeeper mode rejects.
alex: could the adapter coerce casing? lowercase -> uppercase before validation?
maria: we tried `coerce=true` in the adapter but that makes the toolcall appear successful end-to-end. telemetry then undercounts actual rejects and teams lose visibility. billing also sees it as a normal toolcall.
sam: there are two separate concerns: 1) user-facing reliability (we don't want to silently change semantics) and 2) visibility for platform / billing / debug. We should preserve both.
anna: propose adding a "soft_fail" path: when a validation mismatch occurs, return model output with a header `X-Validation-Warning: enum_mismatch` and increment a new metric `toolcall.soft_reject`. That way runtime doesn't break, but we still surface it.
kevin: I like soft_fail for playground/dev routes, but for some critical routes (refunds, payments) we should keep strict mode. Need per-route policy.
infra-bot: Deploy succeeded: gatekeeper-v2 -> prod (by ci/cd). :rocket:
maria: also want richer telemetry: include `validation_reason`, `expected`, `observed_raw_value` in the metric payload. sample raw_value at 1% by default to avoid PII / huge SQS. In canary we can bump sampling.
sam: console UX idea: under model -> toolcalls, show a new card "Recent validation rejects" with top N offending paths and a small sample of raw values (redacted). Add a quick action: [Promote value as accepted enum].
alex: caution: "Promote value" is effectively changing the contract. should require audit + change log and optional webhook to owners. Also might impact billing because a promoted value changes the routing/fallback behaviour.
maria: agreed. promotion should create an internal change request: records who promoted, route, model, and optionally schedule a rollout. For immediate unblock we can have a temporary local override (30 days) that is visible in console.
sam: rollout plan suggestion: 5% canary strict-mode for a subset of routes for 48h, with 100% sampling of validation telemetry for rejects during canary. If reject rate < 0.1% and no human errors, expand.
kevin: technical: we need to change gatekeeper to emit a structured metric `toolcall.validation` with tags {route, model, policy, reason, strictness} and an integer `count`. Also push a small example log line for debugging:
```
{"route":"checkout/refund","model":"redwood-ggml-2","reason":"enum_mismatch","expected":["OK","FAILED"],"observed":"failed","policy":"strict"}
```
anna: UX: console card should allow toggling between strict/lenient for the route, and show a diff preview of what would change if we promote values. Also expose the last 10 rejected payloads (redacted) and a one-click create-change-request button.
maria: items and owners: 1) gatekeeper: emit validation_reason + raw_value sampling -> @kevin 2) metrics + backend: new metric + canary sampling controls -> @sam 3) console: recent rejects card + promote button + audit log -> @anna 4) docs: update strict/soft policy semantics -> @maria
kevin: I'll open the PR for gatekeeper changes. planning a canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC to 5% routes.
maria: good. can we add an emergency circuit: if promote is misused we auto-revert after 24h and send audit alert?
sam: yes, temporary overrides will auto-expire and emit an alert if changed more than X times per hour.
alex: quick example of problematic user output that caused this:
```
{
  "status": "failed",
  "error_code": 502,
  "actions": ["refund"]
}
```
versus schema expecting `status` to be exactly "FAILED".
maria: thanks. I'll post a short howto in #eng-platform with the canary schedule and sample Grafana dashboard widgets to watch. :+1:
kevin: ack.
anna: ack.
maria: closing loop — assigning tasks in the tracker now. ping me if you see any regressions after canary. :eyes:
